title: Node Traversal

story.briefing: The lattice above the network branches in two at every junction. Read it the way the engineers do — left branch first, then the junction itself, then the right.
story.success: Lattice read in order. The junctions report cleanly.

description: Return the values of a binary tree in order: for every node, all of its left subtree first, then the node itself, then all of its right subtree. A tree is given as an array where the node at index i has its left child at index 2i+1 and its right child at index 2i+2. A null entry means there is no node there, and nothing exists beneath it. An empty array is an empty tree.

examples.explanation: No left child, so the root comes first.

hints: The rule for a node is the same as the rule for the whole tree, which is what makes this naturally recursive: handle the left child, record the value, handle the right child.
Two things stop the recursion: running past the end of the array, and landing on a null entry. Check both, or a leaf will send you chasing children that do not exist.

Write a helper taking an index. If the index is out of range or the entry is null, return. Otherwise recurse into 2i+1, append the value, then recurse into 2i+2. Append into one shared array rather than joining new arrays at every step.
